mn9:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthi in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapindika’s Park.
mn9:1.3: There the venerable Sāriputta addressed the bhikkhus thus:
mn9:2.1: ‘“A man of right view” is said, friends.
mn9:2.2: In what way is a noble disciple a man of right view, his view rectified, having perfect [confidence in the Dhamma, this being the true object of faith that he has come to?’
mn9:2.3: ‘Indeed, friend, we would come from far away to learn from the venerable Sāriputta the meaning of this pronouncement.
mn9:2.4: It would be good if the meaning of this pronouncement would occur to the venerable Sāriputta.
mn9:2.5: Having heard it from him, the bhikkhus will remember it.’
mn9:2.6: ‘Then, friends, listen and heed well what I shall say.’
mn9:3.1: ‘As soon as a noble disciple understands the unprofitable, the root of the unprofitable, the profitable, and the root of the profitable,
mn9:3.2: in that way he is a man of right view, his view rectified, having perfect confidence in the Dhamma, this being the true object of faith that he has come to.
mn9:4.1: ‘And what is the unprofitable, the root of the unprofitable; what is the profitable, the root of the profitable?
mn9:4.2: ‘Killing beings is unprofitable. Taking what is not given is unprofitable. Misconduct in sexual desires is unprofitable. False speech is unprofitable. Malicious speech is unprofitable. Harsh speech is unprofitable. Gossip is unprofitable. Covetousness is unprofitable. Ill-will is unprofitable. Wrong view is unprofitable.
mn9:4.3: This is what is called unprofitable.
mn9:5.1: ‘And what is the root of the unprofitable?
mn9:5.2: Greed is a root of the unprofitable. Hate is a root of the unprofitable. Delusion is a root of the unprofitable.
mn9:5.3: This is what is called the root of the unprofitable.
mn9:6.2: Abstention from killing living beings is profitable. Abstention from taking what is not given is profitable. Abstention from misconduct in sexual desires is profitable. Abstention from false speech is profitable. Abstention from malicious speech is profitable. Abstention from harsh speech is profitable. Abstention from gossip is profitable. Abstention from covetousness is profitable. Abstention from ill-will is profitable. Abstention from wrong view is profitable.
mn9:6.3: This is what is called profitable.
mn9:7.1: ‘And what is the root of the profitable?
mn9:7.2: Non-greed is a root of the profitable. Non-hate is a root of the profitable. Non-delusion is a root of the profitable.
mn9:7.3: This is what is called the root of the profitable.
mn9:8.1: ‘After a noble disciple has thus understood the unprofitable, the root of the unprofitable, the profitable and the root of the profitable he entirely abandons the underlying tendency to lust, he abolishes the underlying tendency to resistance, extirpates the underlying tendency to the view and conceit “I am”, and by abandoning ignorance and arousing True Knowledge he here and now makes an end of suffering.
mn9:8.2: In that way a noble disciple is a man of right view, his view is rectified, he has perfect confidence in the Dhamma and this is the true object of faith that he has come to.’
mn9:9.1: Saying, ‘Good, friend,’ the bhikkhus were satisfied and they delighted in the venerable Sāriputta’s words. Then they asked him a further question:
mn9:9.2: ‘But, friend, might there be another way in which a noble disciple is a man of right view, his view rectified, having perfect confidence in the Dhamma, this being the true object of faith that he has come to?’
mn9:10.2: ‘As soon as a noble disciple understands nutriment, the arising of nutriment, the cessation of nutriment, and the way leading to the cessation of nutriment,
mn9:10.3: in that way he is a man of right view, his view is rectified, he has perfect confidence in the Dhamma and this is the true object of faith that he has come to.
mn9:11.1: ‘And what is nutriment, what is the origin of nutriment, what is the cessation of nutriment, what is the way leading to the cessation of nutriment?
mn9:11.2: ‘There are these four kinds of nutriment for the maintenance and support of beings that already exist and for those seeking renewal of being.
mn9:11.4: They are, physical food as nutriment, gross or subtle, contact as the second, volition about (the state of) the mind as the third and consciousness as the fourth.
mn9:11.5: With the arising of craving there is the arising of nutriment. With the cessation of craving there is the cessation of nutriment. The way leading to the cessation of nutriment is just this Noble Eightfold Path, that is to say,
mn9:11.6: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration.
mn9:12.1: ‘After a noble disciple has thus understood nutriment … he entirely abandons the underlying tendency to greed … makes an end of suffering.
mn9:12.2: In that way too a noble disciple is one of right view … and this is the true object of faith that he has come to.’
mn9:13.1: Saying, ‘Good, friend,’ the bhikkhus were satisfied and delighted in the venerable Sāriputta’s words. Then they asked him a further question:
mn9:13.2: ‘But, friend, might there be another way in which a noble disciple is a man of right view … this being the true object of faith that he has come to?’
mn9:14.2: ‘As soon as a noble disciple understands suffering, the origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering and the the way leading to the cessation of suffering,
mn9:14.3: in that way he is a man of right view, his view is rectified, he has perfect confidence in the Dhamma and this is the true object of faith that he has come to.
mn9:15.1: ‘And what is suffering, what is the origin of suffering, what is the cessation of suffering, what is the way leading to the cessation of suffering?
mn9:15.2: ‘Birth is suffering, ageing is suffering, sickness is suffering, death is suffering, sorrow and lamentation, pain, grief and despair are suffering, not to get what one wants is suffering, in short, the five aggregates affected by clinging are suffering.
mn9:15.3: This is what is called suffering.
mn9:16.1: ‘And what is the origin of suffering?
mn9:16.2: It is craving which produces renewed being, is accompanied by delight and lust, delights in this and that, that is to say,
mn9:16.3: craving for sensual desires, craving for being, craving for non-being.
mn9:16.4: This is what is called the origin of suffering.
mn9:17.1: ‘And what is the cessation of suffering?
mn9:17.2: It is the remainderless fading and ceasing, the giving up, relinquishing, letting go and rejecting of that same craving.
mn9:17.3: This is what is called the cessation of suffering.
mn9:18.1: ‘And what is the way leading to the cessation of suffering?
mn9:18.2: It is just this Noble Eightfold Path, that is to say,
mn9:19.1: ‘After a noble disciple has thus understood …
mn9:19.2: he is one of right view … and this is the true object of faith that he has come to.’
mn9:20.1: Saying, ‘Good, friend,’ the bhikkhus were satisfied, and delighted in the venerable Sāriputta’s words. Then they asked him a further question:
mn9:20.2: ‘But, friend, might there be another way in which a noble disciple is a man of right view … this being the true object of faith he has come to?’
mn9:21.2: ‘As soon as a noble disciple understands ageing and death, the origin of ageing and death, the cessation of ageing and death, and the way leading to the cessation of ageing and death,
mn9:21.3: in that way he is a man of right view … and this is the true object of faith that he has come to.
mn9:22.1: ‘But what is ageing and death, what is the origin of ageing and death, what is the cessation of ageing and death, what is the way leading to the cessation of ageing and death?
mn9:22.2: ‘In the various orders of beings, the ageing of beings, their old age, brokenness (of teeth), grayness (of hair), wrinkles, decline of life, and weakness of faculties—
mn9:22.3: that is what is called ageing.
mn9:22.5: ‘In the various orders of beings, the decease, the deceasing, passing-away, dissolution, disappearance, dying, completion of time, dissolution of aggregates—
mn9:22.6: that is what is called death.
mn9:22.9: With the arising of birth there is the arising of ageing-and-death. With the cessation of birth there is the cessation of ageing-and-death. The way leading to the cessation of ageing-and-death is just this Noble Eightfold Path, that is to say,
mn9:23.1: ‘After a noble disciple has thus understood …’
mn9:24.1: Saying, ‘Good, friend,’ the bhikkhus were satisfied, and they delighted in the venerable Sāriputta’s words. Then they asked him a further question:
mn9:24.2: ‘But, friend, might there be another way in which a noble disciple is a man of right view, so that his view is rectified … this being the true object of faith that he has come to?’
mn9:25.2: ‘As soon as a noble disciple understands birth, the origin of birth, the way leading to the cessation of birth,
mn9:25.3: in that way he is one of right view … and this is the true object of faith that he has come to.
mn9:26.1: ‘And what is birth, what is the origin of birth, what is the cessation of birth, what is the way leading to the cessation of birth?
mn9:26.2: ‘In the various orders of beings, the birth of beings, their coming to birth, precipitation (in the womb), generation, manifestation of aggregates, obtaining the bases for contact,
mn9:26.4: With the arising of being there is the arising of birth. With the cessation of being there is the cessation of birth. The way leading to the cessation of birth is just this Noble Eightfold Path, that is to say,
mn9:27.1: ‘After a noble disciple has thus understood …’
mn9:28.1: Saying, ‘Good, friend,’ the bhikkhus were satisfied, and delighted in the venerable Sāriputta’s words. Then they asked him a further question:
mn9:28.2: ‘But, friend, might there be another way in which a noble disciple is a man of right view … this being the true object of faith that he has come to?’
mn9:29.2: ‘As soon as a noble disciple understands being, the origin of being, the cessation of being, the way leading to the cessation of being,
mn9:29.3: in that way he is a man of right view … and this is the true object of faith that he has come to.
mn9:30.1: ‘And what is being, what is the origin of being, what is the cessation of being, what is the way leading to the cessation of being?
mn9:30.2: ‘There are these three kinds of being:
mn9:30.3: sensual desire being, (subtle) form being and formless being.
mn9:30.4: With the arising of clinging there is the arising of being. With the cessation of clinging there is the cessation of being. The way leading to the cessation of being is just this Noble Eightfold Path, that is to say,
mn9:31.1: ‘After a noble disciple has thus understood …’
mn9:32.1: Saying, ‘Good, friend,’ the bhikkhus were satisfied, and delighted in the venerable Sāriputta’s words. Then they asked him a further question.
mn9:32.2: ‘But, friend, might there be another way in which a noble disciple is a man of right view … this being the true object of faith that he has come to?’
mn9:33.2: ‘As soon as a noble disciple understands clinging, the origin of clinging, the way leading to the cessation of clinging,
mn9:33.3: in that way he is a man of right view … and this is the true object of faith that he has come to.
mn9:34.1: ‘And what is clinging, what is the origin of clinging, what is the cessation of clinging, what is the way leading to the cessation of clinging?
mn9:34.2: ‘There are these four kinds of clinging:
mn9:34.3: sensual desire clinging, (false) view clinging, rite and ritual clinging, and self-theory clinging.
mn9:34.4: With the arising of craving there is the arising of clinging. With the cessation of craving there is the cessation of clinging. The way leading to the cessation of clinging is just this Noble Eightfold Path, that is to say,
mn9:35.1: ‘After a noble disciple has thus understood …’
mn9:36.1: Saying, ‘Good, friend,’ the bhikkhus were satisfied, and they delighted in the venerable Sāriputta’s words. Then they asked him a further question:
mn9:36.2: ‘But, [friend, might there be another way in which a noble disciple is a man of right view, his view rectified … this being the true object of faith that he has come to?’
mn9:37.2: ‘As soon as a noble disciple understands craving, the origin of craving, the cessation of craving and the way leading to the cessation of craving,
mn9:37.3: in that way he is a man of right view … and this is the true object of faith that he has come to.
mn9:38.1: ‘And what is craving, what is the cessation of craving, what is the way leading to the cessation of craving?
mn9:38.2: ‘There are these six classes of craving:
mn9:38.3: craving for forms, craving for sounds, craving for odours, craving for flavours, craving for tangibles, craving for dhammas.
mn9:38.4: With the arising of feeling there is the arising of craving. With the cessation of feeling there is the cessation of craving. The way leading to the cessation of craving is just this Noble Eightfold Path, that is to say,
mn9:39.1: ‘After a noble disciple has thus understood …’
mn9:40.1: Saying, ‘Good friend,’ the bhikkhus were satisfied, and delighted in venerable Sāriputta’s words. Then they asked him a further question:
mn9:40.2: ‘But, friend, might there be another way in which a noble disciple is a man of right view … this being the true object of faith that he has come to?’
mn9:41.2: ‘As soon as a noble disciple understands feeling, the origin of feeling, the cessation of feeling, and the way leading to the cessation of feeling,
mn9:41.3: in that way he is a man of right view … and this is the true object of faith that he has come to.
mn9:42.1: ‘And what is feeling, what is the origin of feeling, what is the cessation of feeling, what is the way leading to the cessation of feeling?
mn9:42.2: ‘There are these six classes of feeling:
mn9:42.3: feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, feeling born of tongue-contact, feeling born of body-contact, feeling born of mind contact.
mn9:42.4: With the arising of contact there is the arising of feeling. With cessation of contact there is the cessation of feeling. The way leading to the cessation of feeling is just this Noble Eightfold Path, that is to say,
mn9:43.1: ‘After a noble disciple has thus understood …’
mn9:44.1: Saying, ‘Good, friend,’ the bhikkhus were satisfied, and delighted in the venerable Sāriputta’s words. Then they asked him a further question.
mn9:44.2: ‘But, friend, might there be another way in which a noble disciple is a man of right view … this being the true object of faith that he has come to?’
mn9:45.2: ‘As soon as a noble disciple understands contact, the origin of contact, the cessation of contact, and the way leading to the cessation of contact,
mn9:45.3: in that way he is a man of right view … and this is the true object of faith that he has come to.
mn9:46.1: ‘And what is contact, what is the origin of contact, what is the cessation of contact, what is the way leading to the cessation of contact?
mn9:46.2: ‘There are these six classes of contact:
mn9:46.3: eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, mind-contact.
mn9:46.4: With the arising of the sixfold base there is the arising of contact. With the cessation of the sixfold base there is the cessation of contact. The way leading to the cessation of contact is just this Noble Eightfold Path, that is to say,
mn9:47.1: ‘After a noble disciple has thus understood …’
mn9:48.1: Saying, ‘Good, friend,’ the bhikkhus were satisfied and delighted in the venerable Sāriputta’s words. Then they asked him a further question:
mn9:48.2: ‘But, friend, might there be another way in which a noble disciple is a man of right view … this being the true object of faith which he has come to?’
mn9:49.2: ‘As soon as a noble disciple understands the sixfold base, the origin of the sixfold base, the cessation of the sixfold base, and the way leading to the cessation of the sixfold base,
mn9:49.3: he is a man of right view … and this is the true object of faith that he has come to.
mn9:50.1: ‘And what is the sixfold base, what is the origin of the sixfold base, what is the cessation of the sixfold base, what is the way leading to the cessation of the sixfold base?
mn9:50.3: the eye-base, the-ear base, the nose-base, the tongue-base, the body-base, the mind-base.
mn9:50.4: With the arising of name-and-form there is the arising of the sixfold base. With the cessation of name and-form there is the cessation of the sixfold base. The way leading to the cessation of the sixfold base is just this Noble Eightfold Path, that is to say,
mn9:51.1: ‘After a noble disciple has thus understood …’
mn9:52.1: Saying, ‘Good, friend,’ the bhikkhus were satisfied, and they delighted in the venerable Sāriputta’s words. Then they asked him a further question:
mn9:52.2: ‘But, friend, might there be another way in which a noble disciple is a man of right view … this being the true object of faith which he has come to?’
mn9:53.2: ‘As soon as a noble disciple understands name-and-form, the origin of name-and-form, the cessation of name-and-form, and the way leading to the cessation of name-and-form,
mn9:53.3: in that way he is a man of right view … and this is the true object of faith that he has come to.
mn9:54.1: ‘And what is name-and-form, what is the origin of name-and-form, what is the cessation of name-and-form, what is the way leading to the cessation of name-and-form?
mn9:54.3: these are what is called name.
mn9:54.4: ‘The four great primary elements and the form derived from the four great primary elements,
mn9:54.5: these are what is called form.
mn9:54.8: With the arising of consciousness there is the arising of name-and-form. With the cessation of consciousness there is the cessation of name-and-form. The way leading to the cessation of name-and-form is just this Noble Eightfold Path, that is to say,
mn9:55.1: ‘After a noble disciple has thus understood …’
mn9:56.1: Saying, ‘Good, friend,’ the bhikkhus were satisfied, and they delighted in the venerable Sāriputta’s words. Then they asked him a further question:
mn9:56.2: ‘But, friend, might there be another way in which a noble disciple is a man of right view … this being the true object of faith that he has come to?’
mn9:57.2: ‘As soon as a noble disciple understands consciousness, the origin of consciousness, the cessation of consciousness, and the way leading to the cessation of consciousness,
mn9:57.3: in that way he is a man of right view … and this is the true object of faith that he has come to.
mn9:58.1: ‘And what is consciousness, what is the origin of consciousness, what is the cessation of consciousness, what is the way leading to the cessation of consciousness?
mn9:58.2: ‘There are these six classes of consciousness:
mn9:58.3: eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, mind-consciousness.
mn9:58.4: With the arising of formations there is the arising of consciousness. With the cessation of formations there is the cessation of consciousness. The way leading to the cessation of consciousness is just this Noble Eightfold Path, that is to say,
mn9:59.1: ‘After a noble disciple has thus understood …’
mn9:60.1: Saying, ‘Good, friend,’ the bhikkhus were satisfied and they delighted in the venerable Sāriputta’s words. Then they asked him a further question:
mn9:60.2: ‘But, friend, might there be another way in which a noble disciple is a man of right view ... this being the true object of faith that he has come to?’
mn9:61.2: ‘As soon as a noble disciple understands formations, the arising of formations, the cessation of formations, and the way leading to the cessation of formations,
mn9:61.3: in that way he is a man of right view ... and this is the true object of faith that he has come to.
mn9:62.1: ‘And what are formations, what is the origin of formations, what is the cessation of formations, what is the way leading to the cessation of formations?
mn9:62.2: ‘There are these three kinds of formations:
mn9:62.3: the bodily formation, the verbal formation, the mental formation.
mn9:62.4: With the arising of ignorance there is the arising of formations. With the cessation of ignorance there is the cessation of formations. The way leading to the cessation of formations is just this Noble Eightfold Path, that is to say,
mn9:63.1: ‘After a noble disciple has thus understood ...’
mn9:64.1: Saying, ‘Good, friend,’ the bhikkhus were satisfied, and they delighted in the venerable Sāriputta’s words. Then they asked him a further question:
mn9:64.2: ‘But, friend, might there be another way in which a noble disciple is a man of right view ... this being the true object of faith that he has come to?’
mn9:65.1: ‘As soon as a noble disciple understands ignorance, the origin of ignorance, the cessation of ignorance, and the way leading to the cessation of ignorance,
mn9:65.2: in that way he is a man of right view ... and this is the true object of faith that he has come to.
mn9:65.3: ‘And what is ignorance, what is the origin of ignorance, what is the cessation of ignorance, what is the way leading to the cessation of ignorance?
mn9:65.4: ‘Unknowing about suffering, about the origin of suffering, about the cessation of suffering, about the way leading to the cessation of suffering,
mn9:66.1: With the arising of taints there is the arising of ignorance. With the cessation of taints there is the cessation of ignorance. The way leading to the cessation of ignorance is just this Noble Eightfold Path, that is to say,
mn9:67.1: ‘After a noble disciple has thus understood …’
mn9:68.1: Saying, ‘Good, friend,’ the bhikkhus were satisfied, and they delighted in the venerable Sāriputta’s words. Then they asked him a further question:
mn9:68.2: ‘But, friend, might there be another way in which a noble disciple is a man of right view, his view is rectified, having perfect confidence in the Dhamma, this being the true object of faith that he has come to?’
mn9:69.2: ‘As soon as a noble disciple understands the taints, the origin of taints, the cessation of taints, and the way leading to the cessation of taints,
mn9:69.3: in that way he is a man of right view, his view is rectified, he has perfect confidence in the Dhamma and this is the true object of faith that he has come to.’
mn9:70.1: ‘And what are the taints, what is the origin of taints, what is the cessation of taints, what is the way leading to the cessation of taints?
mn9:70.3: the taint of sensual desires, the taint of being, and the taint of ignorance.
mn9:70.4: With the arising of ignorance there is the arising of taints. With the cessation of ignorance there is the cessation of taints. The way leading to the cessation of taints is just this Noble Eightfold Path, that is to say,
mn9:70.5: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration.’
mn9:71.1: ‘After a noble disciple has thus understood the taints, the origin of taints, the cessation of taints, and the way leading to the cessation of taints, he entirely abandons the underlying tendency to lust, he abolishes the underlying tendency to resistance, extirpates the underlying tendency to the view and conceit “I am”, and by abandoning ignorance and arousing True Knowledge he here and now makes an end of suffering.
mn9:71.2: In that way too a noble disciple is a man of right view, his view is rectified, he has perfect confidence in the Dhamma and this is the true object of faith that he has come to.’
mn9:71.3: That is what the venerable Sāriputta said.
mn9:71.4: The bhikkhus were satisfied, and they delighted in the venerable Sāriputta’s words.
